messages.content: RDU is off my plate now, and a Chicago conference just landed. Can you help me frame the travel before I send anything for approval?
Yes. I can help map the decision points first. What are the conference dates, where in Chicago, and are you trying to arrive the day before or the morning it starts?

It runs Tuesday June 23 through Friday June 26. Healthcare interoperability conference. I am solo, coworkers book separately. The exact venue is around the conference shuttle route, but the employer hotel block is partly waitlisted.
Got it. The two big forks are Monday versus Tuesday arrival, and ORD versus MDW. Do you already know the first required Tuesday session time and the Friday closing time?

That is the annoying part. Organizer has not confirmed if Monday evening networking matters. Tuesday morning might start early but I do not know yet. I do know I do not want a brutally early ATL departure if I can avoid it.

Then I would not commit to a Tuesday-morning flight yet. If there is any early Tuesday requirement, a Monday late-morning or midday flight into Chicago will be much safer and still avoids a pre-dawn start.
For Friday, I want to come back after the closing sessions. Not necessarily late at night, but I do not want to leave before the actual program ends.

That points to return options after roughly midafternoon, assuming the closing session ends around noon or early afternoon. If the agenda includes vendor conversations after the formal close, a later Friday nonstop may be cleaner.
What should I ask about ORD versus Midway? I have not flown into Chicago for work in a while.

Ask which airport the conference shuttle or hotel transfer guidance is built around, and compare the actual door-to-door timing. ORD will usually give more ATL nonstop choices, including midday windows. MDW can be convenient for parts of the city, but a connection or rush-hour arrival could erase the savings.
Hotel-wise, I need something well reviewed and near the shuttle route. If the block does not clear, I need a backup area.

I would shortlist in this order: first, the attached or official conference hotel if the rate is approvable; second, a South Loop or McCormick Place-area hotel on the shuttle route; third, a Loop hotel only if the shuttle pickup is easy. I would verify customer rating, breakfast status, and on-site or nearby dinner options rather than assuming the block hotel covers everything.
Could you give me a compact approval prep list? I am not ready to book, just want to know what to chase down.

Sure. Tentative direction: hold off on ticketing until the Tuesday start is confirmed; favor Monday late morning or midday ATL-Chicago if there is an early Tuesday session; look first at ORD nonstop options, with MDW only if it is clearly cheaper and not a rush-hour mess; return Friday after the closing block, probably midafternoon or later.
And what are the exact open items?

Open items to chase: 1. first required Tuesday session time; 2. whether Monday evening networking is expected or optional; 3. Friday closing time and whether vendor follow-ups matter; 4. venue or shuttle hotel list; 5. whether the employer block can clear and at what rate; 6. whether ORD or MDW is recommended by the organizer; 7. breakfast inclusion and restaurant access for any hotel outside the block; 8. approval threshold for a conference hotel exception.

messages.content: Update on Chicago: the Tuesday 9:00 a.m. implementation roundtable is required, so I need to arrive Monday. Can we compare the real flight and hotel choices now?
Yes. Monday arrival is now the anchor. Send me the flight choices and the hotel rates you are seeing, and I will lay out the tradeoffs for approval.

The travel tool shows a Monday late-morning Delta nonstop ATL to ORD, arriving early afternoon. There is a cheaper one-stop into Midway, but it lands around rush hour. There is also an evening nonstop that gets in late enough that the first night feels compressed.

For the outbound, I would rank them: 1. late-morning nonstop to ORD, cleanest and leaves setup time; 2. evening nonstop, acceptable but compressed; 3. one-stop to MDW, only if cost pressure is strong because the connection plus rush-hour arrival adds risk.
That is my instinct too. The one-stop is about $95 cheaper, not hundreds.

Then the $95 savings is not very compelling for a work conference with a 9:00 a.m. Tuesday start. The late-morning nonstop also reduces the chance you are checking in after dinner and scrambling Tuesday morning.
Friday has two nonstops back. One leaves midafternoon and one leaves later. The midafternoon works only if I leave soon after the closing session.

I would treat the midafternoon return as workable but brittle. If the formal closing ends near noon and you leave by about 12:45, it should be fine. If you want room for vendor conversations, hallway follow-ups, or a slow shuttle, the later nonstop is safer.
I do not love getting home late, but I also do not want to be the person dragging a bag out right after the last slide.
Then the later nonstop fits the trip better unless there is a family or evening constraint at home. It gives you control over the end of the conference without adding a connection.

Hotels: attached conference hotel is 4.5 guest rating, on-site restaurant, attached to the meeting area, but breakfast is paid. Nearby suite property is 4.3, breakfast included, but it is a longer walk or shuttle. Loop hotel is 4.2, lots of restaurants, less convenient for morning sessions.

Side by side: attached hotel gives the lowest morning friction and easiest late arrival, but costs more and breakfast is not included. Suite property saves some money and includes breakfast, but adds daily transfer time. Loop hotel is best for restaurants after hours, but weakest for the 9:00 a.m. roundtable and shuttle dependence.
The attached rate is $278 before taxes. Suites are $229. Loop is about $209. Our policy is usually $250 unless there is a conference exception.

I would ask for the conference exception on the attached hotel and name the suite property as the backup. The justification is not luxury; it is schedule protection: attached meeting access, fewer shuttle variables, on-site dining, and less risk for early sessions.
Does the paid breakfast weaken that recommendation?

It is a downside, but I would not let it outweigh the attached location for this specific agenda. If breakfast is a concern for approval, note that you can use nearby cafes or expense a modest breakfast; if the exception is denied, the suite property becomes the best value because breakfast is included.
What about the Loop hotel? It is tempting because the area is easier for dinner.

I would put it third. It solves dinner but creates morning uncertainty. For a conference where the first required item is at 9:00 and shuttle timing matters, I would rather have on-site dining at the attached hotel or use the suite backup near the shuttle.
Okay. Can you package this for manager approval with a clear preferred option and fallback?

Preferred package: Monday late-morning Delta nonstop ATL to ORD, arriving early afternoon; Friday later nonstop ORD to ATL, to avoid rushing out after closing; attached conference hotel for Monday through Thursday nights, using the conference exception rate because it is directly connected, highly rated, and has on-site dining. Fallback: same flights if possible, but book the nearby suite property with included breakfast if the attached rate is not approved.
Add that I am okay with economy, and if we get to seat selection I would like window seats. Not worth paying just to move forward.

Added. Approval note: Maya should book economy on the Monday late-morning ATL-ORD nonstop and the later Friday ORD-ATL nonstop, with window seats requested when available. Hotel request is the attached 4.5-rated conference hotel despite paid breakfast, because it protects the Tuesday 9:00 start and reduces shuttle risk; if the $278 pre-tax rate is not approved, use the 4.3-rated nearby suite hotel with included breakfast as the fallback.

messages.content: Manager approved the Chicago plan: Monday late-morning nonstop and the attached hotel. But fare hold expires tonight, and product team just added a Friday 1:30 to 2:30 meetup.
That changes the return decision. With a 2:30 end, the midafternoon nonstop is too tight unless you leave early. I would switch the hold to the later nonstop if it is still available.
Agreed. To be clear, I am arriving Monday June 22 for the Tuesday June 23 start, and checking out Friday June 26.

Perfect. Booking frame: ATL to ORD Monday June 22 late morning, arrive early afternoon; ORD to ATL Friday June 26 on the later nonstop after the product meetup; hotel Monday night through Thursday night, checkout Friday.
Seat map is not great. Outbound has 25A and 26F left for windows. Return has 28A and 30F. Forward economy is mostly aisles or middles, and the paid upgrade does not seem worth it.
I would take the window seats over a forward aisle or middle. Choose 25A outbound and 28A return if they are available; skip the paid forward move unless a free better window opens after ticketing.
Yes, window over forward is fine here.
Noted. I would also recheck the seat map after ticketing and again at online check-in, because a better no-fee window may open.
For the hotel, they can add a quiet room away from elevators. Breakfast is still paid. There are cafes in the conference center area, I think.

Add the quiet-room-away-from-elevators request. I would not add a high-floor request unless you care; keeping the note simple makes the important part clearer. For mornings, plan on the conference cafe or a nearby quick breakfast rather than assuming the hotel rate includes it.
No high floor. Can you draft the final booking instructions before I click?

Use this: book economy ATL-ORD on Monday June 22 on the approved late-morning nonstop, and ORD-ATL Friday June 26 on the later nonstop, not the midafternoon return, because of the 1:30-2:30 product meetup. Select 25A outbound and 28A return if still open; otherwise any no-fee window seat before aisle or middle.
The later return shown now is 6:15 p.m. out of ORD, landing ATL at 9:20. The old midafternoon one was 3:25.
Then 6:15 p.m. is the right one. A 3:25 departure would leave almost no buffer after a 2:30 meeting, especially with luggage, airport transfer, security, and possible conference delays.
Anything else I should check before submitting?

Final checks: confirm the fare hold converts before tonight's expiration; verify the ticket still says nonstop both ways; book the attached conference hotel for June 22-26 with the quiet-room-away-from-elevators note; confirm breakfast is not included so expenses are handled correctly; save the hotel confirmation and seat assignments; and recheck seats at check-in for any better free window.
